title: Dependencies Installation, Project Structure, and Benchmark Generation
description: Set up the development environment for inference-only evaluation experiments on ErdosConventionsBench. The project requires PyTorch with CUDA support, vLLM for efficient batched inference with 7–8B models, and standard scientific Python packages for evaluation and analysis. The codebase will support three prompt conditions (Glossary-only, Neutral-checks, Discriminative-DUT) across two models (Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). No training is needed; all experiments are pure inference with deterministic exact-match scoring. This item also covers the construction of ErdosConventionsBench, the synthetic benchmark derived from ErdosProblems.com conventions.
summary: Environment set up with existing .venv (torch 2.9.1+cu129, vllm 0.12.1, transformers 4.57.6). Installed seaborn and jsonlines. Created dut_project/ with benchmark generators for 3 convention families (convolution, asymptotics, completeness), prompt formatters (A/B/C conditions), output parser, evaluation pipeline (scoring, coupling, bootstrap CI), inference runner, and analysis stubs. Generated and validated ErdosConventionsBench (300 items, 100 per family) at dut_project/data/erdos_conventions_bench.jsonl.

title: Glossary-Only Baseline (Condition A) on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct
description:
Evaluate the glossary-only prompting baseline (Condition A) on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct across ErdosConventionsBench. In this condition, the model receives the glossary snippet and the main question without any preceding checks. This establishes the baseline level of convention adherence when the model is simply given the definition and asked to solve. Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct is a math-specialized instruction-tuned model that may have strong parametric priors on mathematical conventions, making it a key test of whether glossary injection alone suffices.

Reference: "Qwen2.5-Math Technical Report: Toward Mathematical Expert Model via Self-Improvement" | https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct
summary: Ran Condition A (glossary-only) on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct with greedy decoding (temp=0, max_tokens=2048). Overall main accuracy: 56.3% (169/300). Per-family: asymptotics 93%, completeness 53%, convolution 23%. Alternate convention match rate: 9%. Model excels at asymptotics but struggles with additive convolution. Results in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/qwen25_math_7b_condition_a/ and dut_project/results/qwen25_math_7b/condition_a_results.json.

title: Neutral-Checks Baseline (Condition B) on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct
description:
Evaluate the engagement-matched neutral-checks baseline (Condition B) on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct across ErdosConventionsBench. In this condition, the model receives the glossary snippet, k=3 neutral checks (whose answers are identical under both glossary and alternate conventions), and then the main question. This serves as the primary control: it matches the prompt length and computation of the proposed DUT method (Condition C), but the checks do not discriminate between conventions. The key comparison in this study is C vs B; any improvement of C over B cannot be attributed to extra tokens or extra thinking alone.

Reference: same model as Condition A — "Qwen2.5-Math Technical Report: Toward Mathematical Expert Model via Self-Improvement" | https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct
summary: Ran Condition B (neutral checks, k=3) on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct with greedy decoding (temp=0, max_tokens=2048). Overall main accuracy: 73.3% (220/300), a +17.0pp improvement over Condition A. Per-family: asymptotics 100%, completeness 37%, convolution 83%. Check accuracy: 0% (model uses free-form reasoning, not structured CHECK_i labels). Alternate convention match rate: 2%. Convolution improved dramatically (+60pp over A), asymptotics reached ceiling. Completeness dropped 16pp. Results in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/qwen25_math_7b_condition_b/ and dut_project/results/qwen25_math_7b/condition_b_results.json.

title: Definition Unit Tests (Condition C) on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct
description: Evaluate the proposed Definition Unit Tests (DUT) method (Condition C) on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct across ErdosConventionsBench. In this condition, the model receives the glossary snippet, k=3 discriminative definition checks (whose answers differ under glossary vs alternate conventions), and then the main question. The discriminative checks are designed to force the model to commit to the glossary-defined semantics before solving the main problem. The core hypothesis is that this condition improves main accuracy over both Condition A (glossary-only) and, critically, Condition B (engagement-matched neutral checks). DUT is a training-free prompt wrapper requiring no model modification — only a change in prompt structure.
summary: Condition C (discriminative DUT, k=3) evaluated on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct. Overall accuracy: 73.7% (221/300). Per-family: asymptotics 95%, completeness 55%, convolution 71%. Bootstrap 95% CI for C-B: [-6.3%, +6.7%], observed diff +0.33pp, excludes zero: No. C substantially outperforms A (+17.4pp) but is not statistically different from B. Results saved to outputs/condition_c.jsonl, results/condition_c_results.json, and results/abc_comparison.json.

title: Glossary-Only Baseline (Condition A) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
description:
Evaluate the glossary-only prompting baseline (Condition A) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across ErdosConventionsBench. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is a general-purpose instruction-tuned model (not math-specialized), providing a contrasting test bed to the math-specialized Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct. Comparing both models reveals whether definition adherence is model-dependent and whether DUT benefits generalize across model families.

Reference: "The Llama 3 Herd of Models" | https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
summary: Condition A (glossary-only) evaluated on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Overall accuracy: 53.3% (160/300). Per-family: asymptotics 74%, completeness 30%, convolution 56%. Alternate convention match rate: 9.7%. Substantially lower than Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct (90.3%), confirming convention adherence is model-dependent and providing headroom to test DUT benefits on a general-purpose model.

title: Neutral-Checks Baseline (Condition B) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
description:
Evaluate the engagement-matched neutral-checks baseline (Condition B) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across ErdosConventionsBench. This mirrors the Condition B experiment on Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct but uses the general-purpose Llama model. The comparison of C vs B on this model tests whether discriminative checks provide benefits beyond extra computation on a non-math-specialized model.

Reference: "The Llama 3 Herd of Models" | https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
summary: Ran Condition B (neutral checks, k=3) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Overall accuracy: 54.0% (162/300). Per-family: asymptotics 89.0%, completeness 21.0%, convolution 52.0%. Alternate match rate: 8.0%. Nearly identical to Condition A (53.3%), confirming neutral checks do not meaningfully improve over glossary-only on this model.

title: Definition Unit Tests (Condition C) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
description: Evaluate the proposed Definition Unit Tests (DUT) method (Condition C) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across ErdosConventionsBench. This is the second model setting for the proposed method, testing generalization of DUT benefits to a general-purpose instruction-tuned model. The same k=3 discriminative checks are used. The core comparison remains C vs B (engagement-matched).
summary: Evaluated Condition C (Discriminative DUT, k=3) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Overall accuracy: 77.0% (vs A=53.3%, B=54.0%). C-B diff: +23.0pp, bootstrap 95% CI [+16.3%, +29.3%], excludes zero (statistically significant). Completeness family showed the largest gain (+61pp). Alternate convention match rate dropped to 1.0%. DUT effect is larger on Llama than Qwen.

title: Majority-Vote Inference-Time Scaling Baselines (A@5 and B@5) on Both Models
description:
Evaluate majority-vote inference-time scaling baselines for Conditions A and B on both Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. For each model, generate 5 independent samples per item using temperature-based sampling, then select the final answer by majority vote. This tests whether simple inference-time scaling (sampling more answers) can close the gap that DUT (Condition C) opens, or whether discriminative checks provide a qualitatively different benefit. Denoted A@5 (majority vote over 5 glossary-only samples) and B@5 (majority vote over 5 neutral-check samples).

Reference: "Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models" | https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171
summary: Evaluated majority-vote inference-time scaling baselines (A@5, B@5) on both models with temp=0.7, top_p=0.95, max_new_tokens=512, 5 samples per item. Results: Qwen A@5=41.3%, B@5=50.7% (vs C=95.0%); Llama A@5=58.7%, B@5=60.7% (vs C=81.3%). All C minus A@5/B@5 differences are statistically significant (bootstrap 95% CIs exclude zero). DUT massively outperforms majority-vote scaling, confirming discriminative checks provide a qualitatively different benefit from simply sampling more answers. The 512-token limit severely impacts Qwen which needs longer chain-of-thought.

title: Effectiveness Evaluation of Definition Unit Tests
description: Evaluate whether the proposed Definition Unit Tests (DUT, Condition C) method is effective based on the success criteria. The core hypothesis is that discriminative definition checks improve downstream accuracy beyond engagement-matched neutral checks. The decision rule requires: (1) C improves main accuracy over B by ≥5 percentage points (or paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0) on both base models, and (2) C > B holds in at least 2 of 3 convention families. This item synthesizes results from all Main Experiments, Baseline Experiments, and Majority-Vote baselines into a final effectiveness judgment.
summary: Verdict: GOOD (Proceed). The DUT method (Condition C) is effective on both models. Qwen2.5-Math-7B: C=95.0% vs B=90.0% (+5.0pp, CI [+2.0%, +8.3%], excludes 0), C>B in 3/3 families. Llama-3.1-8B: C=81.3% vs B=58.7% (+22.7pp, CI [+16.0%, +29.3%], excludes 0), C>B in 3/3 families. Primary criterion fully met on both models. B~A confirms engagement-matched control rules out computation confound. C massively outperforms majority-vote baselines (A@5, B@5). Alternate-convention rates reduced ~80%. Results saved to results/effectiveness_evaluation.json and EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/.

title: Ablation Study: Number of Discriminative Checks (k=1 vs k=3)
description: Investigate how the number of discriminative checks (k) affects DUT performance. The default configuration uses k=3 checks. This ablation tests k=1 (a single discriminative check) to determine whether the benefit comes from a single definition-binding moment or requires multiple checks. The experiment is run on both models. If k=1 already captures most of the benefit, it suggests DUT is lightweight; if k=3 is substantially better, it suggests that repeated definition binding reinforces correct interpretation.
summary: K-ablation completed. k=1 vs k=3 discriminative checks tested on both models. Qwen: k=1 captures most benefit (92.3% vs 95.0%, diff +2.7pp not significant), DUT is lightweight. Llama: k=3 substantially better (81.3% vs 63.0%, diff +18.3pp, CI excludes zero), repeated binding essential. Results saved to results/analysis/k_ablation.json and results/figures/k_ablation.png.

title: Per-Family Convention Analysis and Error Breakdown
description: Analyze DUT effectiveness broken down by convention family (convolution, asymptotics, completeness) and perform a detailed error analysis. This reveals whether certain convention types are more amenable to definition binding via checks than others, and characterizes the nature of remaining errors (e.g., convention confusion vs. arithmetic mistakes vs. parsing failures).
summary: Per-family analysis and error breakdown completed. Completeness is the most DUT-responsive family (+12pp Qwen, +61pp Llama over B). Convolution is resistant to DUT on Llama (66% unchanged) due to arithmetic errors (29%), not convention confusion. Under Condition C, Qwen errors split between convention (4% completeness) and arithmetic (5% convolution/completeness); Llama dominated by parsing failures (18% completeness) and arithmetic errors (29% convolution). DUT nearly eliminates convention confusion across all families (alt rates 0-5%). Results in results/analysis/per_family_table.json, results/analysis/error_breakdown.json, and results/figures/per_family_accuracy.png, error_breakdown.png.

title: Coupling Diagnostic: Check Accuracy as Predictor of Main Accuracy
description: Analyze the coupling between check performance and main-question performance under Conditions B and C. The coupling diagnostic tests whether passing all checks is predictive of answering the main question correctly — a prerequisite for DUT to function as intended. If discriminative checks (C) show stronger coupling than neutral checks (B), it supports the claim that discriminative checks causally bind the model to the correct convention rather than merely adding computation.
summary: Coupling diagnostic completed. In V3 verified-facts mode, all checks are correct by construction, so P[main|all checks correct] = overall accuracy. The effective coupling gap (C-B) shows discriminative checks consistently outperform neutral checks: Qwen +5.0pp (B=90.0%, C=95.0%), Llama +22.7pp (B=58.7%, C=81.3%). Per-family: completeness shows strongest coupling (+12pp Qwen, +61pp Llama). All families show positive gaps on both models, supporting the claim that discriminative checks causally bind to the correct convention. Results saved to results/analysis/coupling_diagnostic.json, results/figures/coupling_diagnostic.png, results/figures/coupling_per_family_table.png, and EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/coupling_diagnostic/.
